text:
She is a beautiful woman of splendid bearing,
Who lets her hair trail in wine.
The claws of love, the poisons of the brothel,
Slip over her granite skin without entering.

She mocks Death and Debauchery:
The monsters whose tearing, rough hand
Has always respected, in its fatal games,
The rude majesty of that proud body.

She walks like a goddess, reclines like a sultana;
A Mohammedan faith she puts in pleasure
And with open arms that set off her breasts,
With her gaze invites the mortal race.

She believes—or better, knows—this barren virgin,
Necessary nevertheless in the march of the world,
That physical beauty is a sublime gift
Able to obtain pardon for every infamy.

She knows neither Hell nor Purgatory,
And when the hour comes to enter Night,
She will look full at Death’s face,
Like a newborn—without hate or regret.

translation.title: Allegory
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire’s French original.
